Use only if clearly needed; limited human data
No data in renal impairment; caution

summary: Nitazoxanide is an FDA-approved thiazolide antiprotozoal indicated for diarrhoea caused by Giardia lamblia or Cryptosporidium parvum in patients 1 year and older. Adults and children >=12 years take 500 mg twice daily for 3 days with food; younger children use weight/age-based oral suspension. It has not been shown effective for cryptosporidiosis in immunocompromised/HIV patients.
indications: Treatment of diarrhoea caused by Giardia lamblia (>=1 year)
Treatment of diarrhoea caused by Cryptosporidium parvum (>=1 year, immunocompetent)

dosage.d: 500 mg (one tablet) every 12 hours for 3 days
dosage.n: Take with food; tablet not for children <=11 years

dosage.d: 200 mg (10 mL suspension) every 12 hours for 3 days
100 mg (5 mL suspension) every 12 hours for 3 days

admin: Tablets (500 mg) must not be given to children 11 years or younger - use the oral suspension
Shake the oral suspension well; reconstitute per instructions and discard after 7 days
moa: Nitazoxanide and its active metabolite tizoxanide interfere with the pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) enzyme-dependent electron-transfer reaction essential to anaerobic energy metabolism in protozoa and anaerobic bacteria, killing the organisms.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to nitazoxanide or any component
relative: Use of tablet form in children <=11 years (overdose risk)

preg: Limited human data; animal studies did not show fetal harm. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether nitazoxanide is excreted in human milk; use caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: Pharmacokinetics have not been studied in renal impairment; use with caution.
hepatic: Pharmacokinetics have not been studied in hepatic impairment; use with caution.

moderate: Highly protein-bound drugs with narrow therapeutic index (e.g. warfarin) - tizoxanide is highly (>99%) protein bound; competition is possible, monitor
interactions.food: Take with food, which increases absorption of the active metabolite.

monitoring: Resolution of diarrhoea and infecting-organism clearance
Hydration and electrolyte status, especially in children
counsel: Take with food and finish the full 3-day course
Your urine may turn bright yellow - this is harmless
Maintain fluids to prevent dehydration from diarrhoea
Children 11 and under must use the liquid, not the tablet
Contact your doctor if diarrhoea persists beyond the course
pk: Tizoxanide peaks ~1-4 h after a dose with food
Store at 20-25 C; reconstituted suspension discard after 7 days
pearls: FDA-approved thiazolide - first-line oral option for giardiasis and immunocompetent cryptosporidiosis
Not shown effective for cryptosporidiosis in HIV/immunocompromised patients
Always take with food to enhance absorption
Tablets contain more drug than paediatric dosing - never give tablets to children <=11 years
Harmless bright-yellow urine discoloration is common
missed: Take the missed dose with food as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and continue the twice-daily schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience. Manage with supportive care and gastric decontamination if appropriate; nitazoxanide is highly protein bound so is unlikely to be efficiently dialysable.
